title: write-before-ioctl key import: correct for variable-length keys
description: KEY_IMPORT uses write(2) to accumulate key bytes before the ioctl, rather than embedding key bytes in the ioctl struct. This avoids a worst-case ioctl struct of 8192 bytes (ML-DSA-87: 4896 bytes + headroom) on the kernel stack for every import call including tiny EC keys. The write-before-ioctl pattern allocates exactly what the key requires on the heap, zeroes it after import. A reviewer who suggests embedding the key in the ioctl struct to 'simplify the API' is wrong.
